*project setup*
import libraries
```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import statsmodels.api as sm
import bambi as bmb
import arviz as az
import polars as pl
from pyprojroot.here import here
from plotnine import *
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
```

import data file
```{python}
snow_data = pl.read_excel(
    here('D:\CoursesUSU\Final_Semester\Intro_Reg_ML\DATA5600\data-5600\Project1\Data-5600-Project-1\OnTheSnow_v1.xlsx')
)
snow_data=snow_data.select(['city','Snow Making','daysOpenLastYear','Runs','averageSnowfall', 'Sentiment'])

#create a region 
snow_data = snow_data.with_columns(
    pl.when(
        pl.col("city").is_in([
            "Utah", "Idaho", "Montana", "Wyoming", "Colorado",
            "New Mexico", "Arizona", "Nevada", "Sierra Nevada",
            "Salt Lake City"
        ])
    ).then(pl.lit("Mountain"))

    .when(
        pl.col("city").is_in([
            "Washington", "Oregon", "Alaska", "Mt. Hood"
        ])
    ).then(pl.lit("West"))

    .when(
        pl.col("city").is_in([
            "Minnesota", "Wisconsin", "Michigan", "Illinois",
            "Indiana", "Ohio", "Iowa", "South Dakota", "Missouri"
        ])
    ).then(pl.lit("Midwest"))

    .when(
        pl.col("city").is_in([
            "New York", "Pennsylvania", "New Jersey", "Connecticut",
            "Massachusetts", "Vermont", "New Hampshire", "Maine",
            "Maryland", "Virginia", "West Virginia",
            "North Carolina"
        ])
    ).then(pl.lit("East"))

    .otherwise(pl.lit("Other"))
    .alias("region")
)

#drop city column
snow_data = snow_data.drop("city")

#drop nulls and nans
snow_data = snow_data.drop_nulls(['Snow Making','daysOpenLastYear','Runs','averageSnowfall', 'Sentiment']) 
snow_data = snow_data.drop_nans(['Snow Making','daysOpenLastYear','Runs','averageSnowfall','Sentiment']) 

snow_data.head()
snow_data["region"].value_counts().sort("count")
```

fit OLS and collect residuals
```{python}
# Dummy code discrete predictors- use east as reference case becuase it has the most entries
snow_train = (snow_data
.to_dummies(columns = ['region'], drop_first = False)
.select(pl.exclude('region_East'))
)

# fit a model
fit_01 = smf.ols(
    "Sentiment ~ 1 + snow_making + days_open_last + runs + avgsnow + region_Midwest + region_Mountain + region_Other + region_West",
    data = snow_train
).fit()

#save residuals
snow_train = (snow_train
  .with_columns(residuals_01 = pl.Series(fit_01.resid))
  .with_columns(fitted_values_01 = pl.Series(fit_01.fittedvalues))
  .with_row_index('observation')
)
```

*exercise_7: exploring residuals*
LINEARITY:
```{python}
(ggplot(
    snow_train, 
    aes(
      x = 'residuals_01', 
      y = 'fitted_values_01'
    )
  )
  + geom_point(alpha = 0.25)
  + geom_smooth(
    method = 'lowess', 
    color = 'red'
  )
  + labs(
    title = 
      'Linearity: Residuals vs. Fitted Values',
    subtitle = 
      'Look for a roughly horizontal line'
  )
)
```

INDEPENDENCE:
```{python}
(ggplot(
    snow_train, 
    aes(x = 'observation', y = 'residuals_01')
  )
  + geom_line(alpha = 0.5)
  + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = 'red')
  + labs(
    title = 
      'Independence: Sequential Residuals',
    subtitle = 
      'Look for a trend in mean or variance'
  )
)
```

CONSTANT VARIANCE:
```{python}
(ggplot(
    snow_train, 
    aes(
      x = 'residuals_01', 
      y = 'fitted_values_01'
    )
  )
  + geom_point(alpha = 0.25, color = 'red')
  + labs(
    title = 
      'Constant Variance: Residuals vs. Fitted Values',
    subtitle = 
      'Look for a funnel shape in the residuals'
  )
)
```

NORMALITY:
```{python}
(ggplot(
    snow_train, 
    aes(sample = 'residuals_01')
  )
  + stat_qq(alpha = 0.25)
  + stat_qq_line(color = 'red')
  + labs(
    title = 'Normality: Q-Q Plot',
    subtitle = 
      'Points should follow the diagonal',
    x = 'Theoretical Quantiles',
    y = 'Sample Quantiles'
  )
)
```

MULTICOLINEARITY / IDENTIFIABILITY:
```{python}
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor

snow_train.columns
predictors = [
  'Snow Making',
 'daysOpenLastYear',
 'Runs',
 'averageSnowfall',
 'region_Midwest',
 'region_Mountain',
 'region_Other',
 'region_West',
]

X_train = snow_train.select(predictors)

pl.DataFrame({
  'predictor': predictors,
  'VIF': [
    variance_inflation_factor(X_train, i)
    for i in range(X_train.shape[1])
  ]
}).sort('VIF', descending = True)
```

```{python}
# Specify the design matrix and outcome
X = snow_train.select(pl.exclude('Sentiment'))
y = snow_train.select('Sentiment')
```

log transformation and quick viz- notice the shape of the data. Do we need a log transform?
```{python}
y_train = (y_train
  .with_columns(
    log_sentiment = (pl.col('Sentiment') + 1).log()
  )
  .select('log_sentiment')
)

(ggplot(y_train, aes(x = 'log_sentiment'))
  + geom_histogram(bins = 10)
)

# Add constant for intercept
X_train = sm.add_constant(X_train)

# Fit the model
fit_04 = sm.OLS(y_train, X_train).fit()
fit_04.summary()

# retrieve untransformed params
coef_table = pl.DataFrame({
    "parameter": fit_04.params.index,
    "log_coef": fit_04.params.values,
    "p_value": fit_04.pvalues.values
})

coef_table = (
    coef_table
    .with_columns(
        ((pl.col("log_coef").exp() - 1) * 100)
        .alias("percent_change")
    )
    .filter(pl.col("parameter") != "const")
)

coef_table
```

```{python}
# Keep only the outcome and our four resort-attribute predictors
```

```{python}
# Specify the outcome

# Split into training and testing sets
```

```{python}
# Snow Making is heavily right-skewed, log transformed to normalize
X_train = (X_train
  .with_columns((pl.col('Snow Making') + 1).log().alias('log_snow_making'))
  .select(pl.exclude('Snow Making'))
  .to_pandas()
)

X_test = (X_test
  .with_columns((pl.col('Snow Making') + 1).log().alias('log_snow_making'))
  .select(pl.exclude('Snow Making'))
  .to_pandas()
)

X_train.head()

```

Initial model 
```{python}
# Add constant for intercept
X_train = sm.add_constant(X_train)

# Fit the model
fit_05 = sm.OLS(y_train.to_pandas(), X_train).fit()
fit_05.summary()

```

```{python}
pl.DataFrame({
  'term': fit_05.params.index.tolist(),

}).filter(pl.col('term') != 'const')
```

 Frequentist Model

```{python}
# Combine the outcome and predictors into one training frame
snow_train = pl.concat([y_train, pl.from_pandas(X_train.drop(columns = 'const'))], how = 'horizontal_extend').to_pandas()

predictors = ['daysOpenLastYear', 'Runs', 'averageSnowfall', 'log_snow_making']

fr_fit = smf.ols(
  'Sentiment ~ ' + ' + '.join(predictors),
  data = snow_train
).fit()

fr_fit.summary()

```

Bayesian Model

```{python}
# Specify a Bayesian linear regression
ba_model = bmb.Model(
  'Sentiment ~ ' + ' + '.join(predictors),
  data = snow_train
)

# Specify priors
priors_dict = {
  'Intercept': bmb.Prior('Uniform', lower = -100, upper = 100),
  **{term: bmb.Prior('Uniform', lower = -100, upper = 100) for term in predictors},
  'sigma': bmb.Prior('Exponential', lam = 1)
}

ba_model.set_priors(priors = priors_dict)
ba_model
```

```{python}
# Fit a Bayesian linear regression
ba_fit = ba_model.fit()
```

```{python}
az.summary(ba_fit, ci_kind = 'hdi', ci_prob = 0.95)
```
